subject: how to remove markers with very low LOD value?

messages.author: 5636faa1208a4d16
messages.subject: how to remove markers with very low LOD value?
parts:
Hi all,

My data set includes 30 thousand SNP markers among 10 chromosomes. After the scanone analysis I want to truncate/remove those markers with pretty low LOD values, say like below 50%. How could I do that?

Also, the summary only shows the marker with the highest lod value in each chromosome, if I have multiple peaks in one chromosome higher than 99%, how can I print them all, with position can lod value just like the summary of scanone do?

Thank you so much for your help!

Anjun

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] how to remove markers with very low LOD value?
parts:
The output of scanone() is a data frame. You can subset the rows as with any other data frame.

data(hyper)
hyper <- calc.genoprob(hyper, step=1)
out <- scanone(hyper)

# rows with LOD > 3
out[out[,3] > 3, ]

karl

Let me try to explain by an example:

out[, 7] returns the 7th column

out[,7]>5 gives a vector of TRUE/FALSE indicating which rows have a value>5 in the 7th column

out[ out[,7]>5, c(1,2,7)]
returns the 1st, 2nd, and 7th columns for the rows where the value in the 7th column is >5.

karl
